title: Integrated in silico and in vitro assessment of estrogen and androgen receptor activity of 10 selected PFAS within an Integrated Approach to Testing and Assessment (IATA).
authors: Ortiz, Darlene Mae D; Lee, Handule; Hoang, Ngoc Minh-Hong; Lee, Hyun Jun; Choi, Jinhee; Park, Kwangsik
one_liner_zh: 该文结合分子对接与体外实验评估PFAS对雌激素/雄激素受体的内分泌干扰活性，虽涉及蛋白-配体对接而非TF-DNA互作，但对接与受体结合建模方法可迁移至TF-DNA研究，属广义蛋白-核酸相关但非核心体系。
abstract: The potential of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) to disrupt endocrine systems continues to be a regulatory concern. However, effectively prioritizing these structurally diverse chemicals remains challenging due to inconsistencies in predictive and experimental data. In this study, we employed a multi-tiered evaluation strategy that combines in silico modeling, in vitro assays, and curated mechanistic data within the OECD's Integrated Approach to Testing and Assessment (IATA) framework. Molecular docking using AutoDock Vina, CB-Dock2, and Endocrine Disruptome consistently revealed strong binding affinities of long-chain PFAS, particularly PFDA, PFOA, and 10:2 FTOH, to estrogen and androgen receptors. These predictions were corroborated by ER and AR transactivation assays (OECD TG 455/458), which demonstrated ER agonist and AR antagonist activity for the same compounds. In contrast, short-chain and sulfonated PFAS (PFHxA, PFBS, PFOS) exhibited limited to no activity across platforms. To enhance the biological relevance of the prioritization, we compiled supporting mechanistic evidence by applying the IATA framework to organize data along the adverse outcome pathway from molecular initiating events, through key events, to predicted adverse outcomes. Literature-reported alterations in steroidogenic enzymes and hormone levels were included to enrich mechanistic depth. All lines of evidences were systematically integrated into a weight-of-evidence matrix, enabling a transparent and biologically plausible ranking of PFAS based on receptor interaction, functional activity, and endocrine-disruptive potential. This combined approach identified PFDA and PFOA as high-priority endocrine disruptors and offers a scalable, non-in vivo strategy for the screening and risk-based prioritization of environmentally persistent chemicals.
abstract_zh: 全氟和多氟烷基物质（PFAS）干扰内分泌系统的潜力持续成为监管关注点。然而，由于预测和实验数据的不一致性，有效优先排序这些结构多样的化学品仍具挑战性。在本研究中，我们采用了一种多层次评估策略，结合了计算机模拟（in silico modeling）、体外实验（in vitro assays）以及经整理的机制性数据，并置于OECD的综合测试与评估方法（IATA）框架内。使用AutoDock Vina、CB-Dock2和Endocrine Disruptome进行的分子对接（molecular docking）一致显示，长链PFAS，特别是PFDA、PFOA和10:2 FTOH，对雌激素和雄激素受体具有强结合亲和力。这些预测通过ER和AR反式激活实验（OECD TG 455/458）得到证实，该实验显示相同化合物具有ER激动剂和AR拮抗剂活性。相比之下，短链和磺化PFAS（PFHxA、PFBS、PFOS）在各平台上表现出有限或无活性。为增强优先排序的生物学相关性，我们通过应用IATA框架，沿不良结局通路（adverse outcome pathway）从分子起始事件、关键事件到预测的不良结局组织数据，汇编了支持性机制证据。文献报道的类固醇生成酶和激素水平变化被纳入以丰富机制深度。所有证据线被系统整合到证据权重矩阵中，从而基于受体相互作用、功能活性和内分泌干扰潜力，实现对PFAS的透明且生物学上合理的排序。这种组合方法将PFDA和PFOA识别为高优先级内分泌干扰物，并提供了一种可扩展、非体内（non-in vivo）的策略，用于环境持久性化学品的筛选和基于风险的优先排序。
